name: Pullover
pattern: Straight-arm shoulder extension: the arms swing from overhead down to the hips or chest with the elbows nearly fixed.
setup: Lie face up on a bench, head supported, feet flat on the floor.
Hold one dumbbell with both hands over your chest, elbows slightly bent.
Ribs down and lower back gently on the bench.

steps.text: Weight over your chest, arms nearly straight.
Keeping the elbow bend fixed, lower the weight in an arc behind your head until your arms are beside your ears.
Stop where you feel a stretch under the arms, ribs still down.
Pull the weight back over your chest along the same arc.

cues.cue: Fix a soft elbow bend; do not bend and press.
cues.why: The moment arm of the load at the shoulder sets which muscle works; bending the elbows shortens it and turns it into a triceps press.

cues.cue: Ribs down, lower back stays on the bench.
cues.why: Arching the back fakes shoulder range; the arms can only reach about as far as your shoulder flexion allows.

cues.cue: Lower until your arms are beside your ears, not further.
cues.why: Above about 150-170° of arm elevation the shoulder runs out of range and the load moves to the joint.

cues.cue: For chest, lie across the bench; for lats, use a cable straight-arm pulldown.
cues.why: The free-weight pullover worked the pectoralis more than the latissimus.

breathing: Breathe in as the weight goes back, out as you pull it over.

tempo.note: Slow arc both ways; short pause in the stretch.

mistakes.name: Back arches
mistakes.looks: The lower back lifts off the bench and the ribs flare as the weight goes overhead.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range and keep your ribs pulled down.
mistakes.why: The spine is bending to finish range the shoulder does not have.

mistakes.name: Elbows bend and press
mistakes.looks: The elbows bend a lot behind the head, then straighten as the weight comes up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the same small elbow bend for the whole arc.
mistakes.why: It turns the pullover into a triceps extension and changes the muscles worked.

mistakes.name: Too deep
mistakes.looks: The weight drops below the bench line and the shoulders feel pinched.
mistakes.fix: Stop when your arms are beside your ears.
mistakes.why: Loading the end of shoulder range strains the joint capsule and rotator cuff.

safety: Shoulder pain or instability: keep the range short, or use a cable straight-arm pulldown.
Hold the dumbbell by the inside of the top plate with both palms; check it is secure.

variants.change: Elbows bent about 60-90°: shorter lever, more weight, more triceps.
Elbows near straight: longer lever, lighter weight.
Head lower than hips: the hardest part moves later in the arc.
Shoulders on a ball, hips up in a bridge: adds glute and trunk work.
Hold the stretched position for time.
Pullover then press: bend the elbows at the chest and press the bar up.

subtypes.name: Straight-arm pulldown
subtypes.change: Standing at a high cable, hips hinged slightly; arms nearly straight sweep from overhead down to the thighs. Lats work most at the end.

motion.basis: Muscle emphasis from marchetti2011; scapular upward rotation with arm elevation (about 45-55° at full elevation) from escamilla2009 and ludewig2009, scaled by us to the arm angle. Bench and leg positions are convention; elbow angle estimated.

sources.cite: Marchetti PH, Uchida MC. Effects of the pullover exercise on the pectoralis major and latissimus dorsi muscles as evaluated by EMG. J Appl Biomech. 2011;27(4):380-384.
Escamilla RF, Yamashiro K, Paulos L, Andrews JR. Shoulder muscle activity and function in common shoulder rehabilitation exercises. Sports Med. 2009;39(8):663-685.
Ludewig PM, Phadke V, Braman JP, Hassett DR, Cieminski CJ, LaPrade RF. Motion of the shoulder complex during multiplanar humeral elevation. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2009;91(2):378-389.
